page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv6 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The server features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 472 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2170.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 31.35 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 3990.17 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 26.15 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is also a limiting factor, with uncached read and write speeds of 37.14 GB/sec and 25.89 GB/sec respectively. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for deep learning operations, though medium-sized LLM inference remains slow, yielding 4.5 tokens/sec for text generation on a 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E8-4ds_v6 offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The combination of 64.0 GB of RAM and a fast 472 GB local NVMe SSD makes this server well-suited for relational databases, caching layers, memory-intensive data processing, and text processing applications.
